name: Rhubarb
grown_as: A hardy perennial grown for its red leaf stalks, which are pulled from April to July, often forced early under a pot. Varieties differ in stalk colour from green to deep red: drawn red. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: A big clump of huge leaves about 1 m high and 1 to 1.5 m across, rising on thick stalks straight from a crown at the soil. A tall flower stem to 2 m may come up in late spring.

leaf.outline: Huge, 30 to 60 cm or more across, broadly heart-shaped to rounded-triangular, slightly wider than long
leaf.base: Deeply heart-shaped, the two lobes either side of the stalk
leaf.margin: Entire but strongly wavy and crimped
leaf.veins: Palmate: five to seven thick pale veins spreading from the top of the stalk, branching outward
leaf.surface: Puckered and blistered between the veins, slightly glossy above, faintly hairy beneath
leaf.stalk: Very thick and fleshy, 30 to 60 cm, flat or grooved on top and rounded beneath, red to pink-green, with a papery brown sheath at the base
leaf.colour: Mid to dark green, the veins paler or reddish

flower.form: A huge branched plume of tiny flowers
flower.colour: Creamy white, sometimes greenish or pink-tinged
flower.behind: Papery sheaths at the stem joints
flower.carried: In dense branched clusters (panicles) on a thick, hollow, upright stem 1.5 to 2 m, held high above the leaves
flower.size: Each flower 2 to 3 mm; the plume 50 cm or more
flower.season: May to June; gardeners usually cut the stem off

fruit: Crop: the red leaf stalks. After flowering: masses of flat, three-winged dry fruits about 1 cm, green turning red-brown.
seedling: Not drawn: grown from divided crowns
winter: Leaves die and collapse in autumn; the bare crown sits at the soil with large rounded pink-red buds

leaf: a huge heart-shaped leaf with a strongly wavy crimped edge
five to seven thick veins spreading from the stalk
crown: a knobbly woody crown at the soil
young: crumpled leaves unfolding from the crown
crop: thick red stalks rising straight from the crown
huge wavy heart-shaped leaves on top
flower: a tall stout stem rising above the leaves
a creamy plume of flowers at the top
dormant: a bare crown at the soil

look_alikes: Butterbur (Petasites hybridus) has big round leaves but they are toothed and grey-downy beneath, with pinkish flower spikes in early spring. Burdock leaves are greyer, woolly beneath with hollow green stalks. Gunnera is far bigger with prickly stalks.
